summary: Nasdaq fell 2.6% (worst day since June) on AI-spending worries led by Meta -7%, while the Dow and Russell finished flat as money rotated and bonds rallied. Brent rose to about $112 on Iran-US escalation fears, the dollar sits near a three-week low, the yen at a one-month high, and gold fell for a fifth straight day.
events_next_24h: Sat 1:00am USD UMich sentiment and inflation expectations
Sat 6:30am CFTC COT report (positioning to 20 Oct)

NQ.why: AI capex fears hit megacaps and chips (Meta -7%, CoreWeave -10%) for the worst day since June, with a hawkish Fed backdrop; positioning is not crowded short.
NQ.risk: A strong rebound in semis or a sharp drop in yields restoring risk appetite.

ES.why: S&P fell 1.2% on the tech drag and oil spike, but the Dow and Russell held flat and leveraged funds are already fairly short (22nd pct).
ES.risk: Rotation keeps the broad tape stable and tech stops falling.

YM.why: Dow closed flat as money rotated out of tech into value and energy, so the risk-off and rotation forces offset.
YM.risk: A broader risk-off leg pulling value names down with tech.

RTY.why: Small caps edged up as yields fell sharply, but a risk-off oil shock and hawkish Fed cut the other way.
RTY.risk: Yields reversing higher, or a clean risk-on bounce lifting small caps.

NKD.why: Nasdaq tech rout and a firmer yen weigh on the Nikkei, already down 2.4% in five days; leveraged funds near the 10th pct short limit conviction.
NKD.risk: Japan CPI at 10:30am or a yen reversal sparking a short-covering bounce.

6J.why: Yen hit a one-month high as the dollar slid to a three-week low, US yields fell and risk appetite soured.
6J.risk: Soft Japan CPI or firm BOJ-hold signals reviving the carry trade.

6E.why: Dollar weakness supports the euro, but French debt worries and next week's ECB meeting keep it capped.
6E.risk: Dollar breaking lower on weak US PMIs, or fresh French fiscal stress.

6B.why: No clear sterling-specific driver found overnight; the softer dollar is offset by risk-off flows.
6B.risk: A decisive US PMI miss or beat moving the dollar.

6A.why: Hawkish RBA talk on oil-driven inflation supports the Aussie, but global risk-off and Asian equity weakness weigh on it.
6A.risk: Asian stocks stabilising, or the sell-off deepening.

ZN.why: Bonds caught a strong haven bid as the 10-year yield fell roughly 10-19bp, though oil-driven inflation and a hawkish Fed limit the upside.
ZN.risk: Oil inflation fears or hot UMich inflation expectations pushing yields back up.

GC.why: Gold fell a fifth straight day as Fed hike bets build, and it slid even with a weaker dollar and Middle East tension.
GC.risk: A major Middle East escalation or a sharp dollar drop driving haven buying.

CL.why: Brent topped $112, a five-month high, after attacks on Saudi oil sites, US embassy departures and reports of post-midterm strike plans on Iran.
CL.risk: De-escalation news or more sanctions relief on Russian energy supply.
